_origin: Entries with "finicky": true come from Finicky's apps/finicky/src/browser/browsers.json (MIT, Copyright (c) 2015-2025 John Sterling); their macOS bundle_id, app_name, engine and profile directory are Finicky's.
Everything else (Windows, Linux, and the browsers Finicky lacks) was added for PwrRoute; each entry's sources say where its facts came from.
Path templates start with a base-directory token; see Env::expand in src/env.rs.

singleton_protocol opts in to a verified wire format; absent, the browser handles its own handoff. Chromium forks may change the header (Edge 156 sends two timestamp fields before argv), so engine is not evidence of compatibility.

private_flag is the engine's by default: Chromium's --incognito (chrome/common/chrome_switches.cc, kIncognito) and Firefox's --private-window (wiki.mozilla.org/Firefox/CommandLineOptions); WebKit browsers have none. An entry sets it only to override: Edge spells it --inprivate, and Arc and Dia take none.

browsers.name: Google Chrome
browsers.notes: Windows per-user installs that do not own the plain registration append '.<suffix>' to the ProgID; it still matches. /usr/bin/google-chrome is shared by every channel's package, so only google-chrome-stable is used.

browsers.name: Google Chrome Beta
browsers.notes: Windows per-user installs that do not own the plain registration append '.<suffix>' to the ProgID; it still matches.

browsers.name: Google Chrome Dev
browsers.notes: Windows per-user installs that do not own the plain registration append '.<suffix>' to the ProgID; it still matches. Linux calls the Dev channel 'unstable'.

browsers.name: Google Chrome Canary
browsers.notes: Windows Canary is per-user only and cannot be the default browser.

browsers.name: Chromium
browsers.notes: ungoogled-chromium shares Chromium's bundle id, ProgID and directories, so it is this entry. Windows per-user installs that do not own the plain registration append '.<suffix>' to the ProgID; it still matches.

browsers.name: Microsoft Edge
browsers.notes: Edge spells the private-window switch --inprivate. /usr/bin/microsoft-edge is shared by every channel's package, so only microsoft-edge-stable is used. Linux profile directories follow Chromium's naming; Microsoft does not document them.

browsers.name: Microsoft Edge Beta
browsers.notes: Edge spells the private-window switch --inprivate. Linux profile directories follow Chromium's naming; Microsoft does not document them.

browsers.name: Microsoft Edge Dev
browsers.notes: Edge spells the private-window switch --inprivate. Linux profile directories follow Chromium's naming; Microsoft does not document them.

browsers.name: Microsoft Edge Canary
browsers.notes: Edge spells the private-window switch --inprivate. Windows Canary is per-user; its ProgID is unverified. Linux profile directories follow Chromium's naming; Microsoft does not document them.

browsers.name: Brave Browser
browsers.notes: The Flatpak (com.brave.Browser) shares the native desktop id. /usr/bin/brave-browser is shared by every channel's package. Windows per-user installs that do not own the plain registration append '.<suffix>' to the ProgID; it still matches.

browsers.name: Brave Browser Beta
browsers.notes: Windows per-user installs that do not own the plain registration append '.<suffix>' to the ProgID; it still matches.

browsers.name: Brave Browser Nightly
browsers.notes: Windows per-user installs that do not own the plain registration append '.<suffix>' to the ProgID; it still matches.

browsers.name: Vivaldi
browsers.notes: The ProgID comes from a deployment script and a forum post, not Vivaldi. Windows per-user installs that do not own the plain registration append '.<suffix>' to the ProgID; it still matches.

browsers.name: Vivaldi Snapshot
browsers.notes: No Windows entry: Snapshot replaces stable in the same directory unless installed standalone, wherever the user chose.

browsers.name: Opera
browsers.notes: Finicky passes --profile-directory to it; Opera does not document the flag (its forums describe --user-data-dir per profile). Windows keeps Opera's data in Roaming; the per-user install path and the Linux profile directory are Opera's defaults, not verified against Opera documentation.

browsers.name: Opera GX
browsers.notes: Finicky passes --profile-directory to it; Opera does not document the flag (its forums describe --user-data-dir per profile). The Windows install path and native Linux profile directory are unverified.

browsers.name: Yandex
browsers.notes: Finicky treats it as Chromium for profiles; Yandex does not document --profile-directory. The Windows executable name and the Flatpak profile directory are unverified.

browsers.name: Wavebox
browsers.notes: Homebrew's quit stanza says io.wavebox.wavebox, but the app's preferences plist and Finicky say com.bookry.wavebox. No Windows entry: its install path is unverified. The Linux profile directory is inferred.

browsers.name: Helium
browsers.notes: Helium's Windows branding keeps chrome.exe; the executable name is inferred from that patch. Windows per-user installs that do not own the plain registration append '.<suffix>' to the ProgID; it still matches.

browsers.name: Comet
browsers.notes: No Linux build. No Windows entry: its install path and user-data directory are unverified.

browsers.name: Ecosia Browser
browsers.notes: The macOS facts are Finicky's alone (no Homebrew cask). Linux: the Flatpak only; the Snap's paths are unverified. No Windows entry: its paths are unverified.

browsers.name: Thorium
browsers.notes: Homebrew installs the bundle as 'Thorium Browser.app'; detection still finds it by bundle id. Windows per-user installs that do not own the plain registration append '.<suffix>' to the ProgID; it still matches.

browsers.name: Arc
browsers.notes: Arc ignores --profile-directory (its Spaces are reachable only from AppleScript); whether it honors --incognito is unverified, so no private-window flag is sent. No Windows entry: it ships as an MSIX package with no fixed executable path. No Linux build.

browsers.name: Dia
browsers.notes: Dia ignores --profile-directory; whether it honors --incognito is unverified, so no private-window flag is sent. No Windows entry (MSIX, early build). No Linux build.

browsers.name: Firefox
browsers.notes: Linux: Firefox 147+ uses $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/mozilla/firefox for new profiles but keeps ~/.mozilla/firefox when it exists, so that is checked first. The Snap keeps the legacy layout (MOZ_LEGACY_HOME). The Flatpak's XDG path is inferred. Every Firefox channel and Gecko fork on Windows may register FirefoxURL-<hash>, so only this entry claims it.

browsers.name: Firefox Developer Edition
browsers.notes: Shares Firefox's profiles.ini; its own default profile is dev-edition-default. Linux: Firefox 147+ uses $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/mozilla/firefox for new profiles but keeps ~/.mozilla/firefox when it exists, so that is checked first.

browsers.name: Firefox Nightly
browsers.notes: Shares Firefox's profiles.ini; its own default profile is default-nightly. Linux: Firefox 147+ uses $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/mozilla/firefox for new profiles but keeps ~/.mozilla/firefox when it exists, so that is checked first.

browsers.name: Zen
browsers.notes: Windows: registers Firefox's FirefoxURL-<hash> ProgID, so it is matched by path. Linux: ~/.config/zen for new profiles comes from a community report. -P is Gecko's flag; the fork does not document it.

browsers.name: Floorp
browsers.notes: The macOS bundle id is unverified, so Floorp is matched by app name. The Windows and native Linux profile directories are unconfirmed for releases. -P is Gecko's flag; the fork does not document it.

browsers.name: LibreWolf
browsers.notes: The aliases are older macOS bundle ids Homebrew still cleans up. Linux: the legacy ~/.librewolf wins when present. -P is Gecko's flag; the fork does not document it.

browsers.name: Waterfox
browsers.notes: Which of the two Windows directories holds profiles.ini is unresolved; the one that has it is used. -P is Gecko's flag; the fork does not document it.

browsers.name: Safari
browsers.notes: Safari 17+ profiles cannot be chosen from the command line.

browsers.name: Orion
browsers.notes: Each Orion profile is a separate app with its own bundle id; a config targets one by that id or path. The Linux beta (a Kagi-hosted Flatpak) is not listed: its ids are unverified.
